t: You're on Princes Gate, a street in London. Three people connected to it are named in the record. Field Marshal Douglas Haig, who commanded the British Expeditionary Force on the Western Front from late 1915 until the end of the First World War, died here. Alexander Shaw, the second Baron Craigmyle, a Scottish Liberal politician, lived here. And Lady Elizabeth Kerr, who lived from 1807 to 1871, also died on this street. So it's a place where a few notable lives ended or were lived out.
